title: Build an image from a Dockerfile, then run it
lead: A small web server with no dependencies, so the build needs nothing but the base image.

steps.note: -t names the image. The dot is the build context: the folder Docker may copy from. --progress=plain prints every step on its own lines; to keep this page short, only the lines that name a step are shown.

title: Two services with Docker Compose
lead: One file describes both containers. The second waits until the first reports healthy, then reaches it by its service name.

extra.compose.yaml:
services:
  web:
    build: ./hello-node
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://localhost:3000"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 15

  probe:
    image: alpine
    depends_on:
      web:
        condition: service_healthy
    command: ["wget", "-qO-", "http://web:3000"]

steps.note: Compose builds web, starts it, waits for its health check, then starts probe.
steps.out:

steps.note: probe runs once and stops. Whether it still shows as Up or already as Exited depends on timing; web stays up and reports healthy.

title: Containers finding each other by name
lead: On the default network, names do not resolve. On a network you create, they do.

steps.cmd: docker run --rm alpine wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://server; echo "exit code: $?"
steps.note: A second container on the default bridge cannot find 'server' by name.

steps.cmd: docker run --rm --network lab-net alpine wget -q -O- http://server2 | head -4
steps.note: On a user-defined network Docker runs a small DNS server, so the container name works as a host name.

steps.out:
NAME      DRIVER    SCOPE
lab-net   bridge    local

title: Data that outlives the container
lead: A container's own files disappear with it. A volume does not.

steps.cmd: docker run --rm -v notes:/data alpine sh -c 'echo saved > /data/hello.txt'
steps.note: The container writes a file into the volume and is removed when it exits.
A new container mounts the same volume and finds the file.

steps.cmd: docker run --rm alpine cat /data/hello.txt; echo "exit code: $?"
steps.note: Without the volume there is nothing there: the first container's file went with it.
steps.out:
exit code: 1
cat: can't open '/data/hello.txt': No such file or directory

title: Swarm: three copies of a service, then a rolling update
lead: A swarm runs a service as several tasks and replaces them one at a time when you update it.

steps.note: This machine becomes a manager. A real cluster also joins other machines with the worker token that init prints.
steps.out: Swarm initialized: current node (lhap4fku5ceh0pl67kczg7d95) is now a manager.

NAME      MODE         REPLICAS   IMAGE
web       replicated   3/3        nginx:1.27-alpine

steps.note: Swarm replaces tasks in turns (parallelism 1 by default). Requests were not sent during the update, so reachability is not shown.

steps.cmd: sleep 25; docker service ps web --filter desired-state=running --format 'table {{.Name}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.CurrentState}}'
